access.accountWall: Straight after the last question of every quiz (step *_step_user, "Almost done! Your details": first name, last name, date of birth, email, password, a GP-information tick, a consent tick with four statements, and an optional newsletter tick). It comes BEFORE any result: the plan choice and the consultation screen are only shown after /quiz/step/register.
blockers: Account wall before results: the recommendation screen and the consultation screen could not be seen live.
Some SKUs in the rules (PHI1220, PHI1221, PHI1306, PHI1307, PHI1309, PHI1749, women's add-ons, scalp products) have no public product page that could be found, so their names are unknown.
access.coverageNote: Stage 1 walked all three quizzes to the account wall and saved the full served quiz definition. Stage 2 replayed the three baselines and 44 variants (42 one-change, 2 deliberate two-change contrasts) (47 replays, runs/b-* , m*, w*, s01), each to the wall. At the wall the site's own client function window.quiz.checkProductAvailability() was run read-only in the live page (scratch/walk-eval.js), which returns the SKUs the results page would list; it matched the Python port of the rules in all 47 runs, so the served rules have not changed. Follow-up questions (show-ifs) were seen live; no answer produced a warning screen, stop screen or different wall before registration. Results screens themselves were not seen (account wall). Stage 3 (independent verify, 24 Nov 2026): 3 fresh baselines and 19 variants (runs/verify-*), 12 of them on options never replayed before, 3 deliberate two-change contrasts; all 22 matched an independent port of the rule check (scratch/verify/engine.js) and the served rules were byte-identical to the saved definitions. 12 product pages, both leaflets and the clinic price list were re-read live.

engineSummary: A rules engine that runs in the browser and is fully visible. Each product SKU has "conditions" (hair-loss picture, density, age, scalp state) that must be true and "blockers" (safety answers) that must all be false; questions are matched by their on-screen label text. The served rules put each passing SKU in a "Recommended" or "Other" group (the rendered results page itself was not seen); if none passes, the person gets the "Choose your consultation type" screen (in-clinic or virtual initial consultation with a booking calendar; the screen shows no price, the clinic price list says virtual from £200, clinic from £345). That is the three-route triage: subscribe (something passes), consultation (everything blocked), or the clinic booking link that skips the quiz. What decides the route: (1) safety answers block everything (men: sudden or not-yet-noticed loss, pain/burning/crusting/bleeding, cancer or PSA monitoring, depression or anxiety, trying for a baby, severe itching or dandruff, allergy to both actives; women: pregnant or breastfeeding, chemotherapy, patches, band-like or other patterns, psoriasis, redness, acne, other or moderate-to-severe scalp symptoms, minoxidil allergy, oral minoxidil); (2) the hair-loss picture picks the product family (men: Temples / Temples and Crown / Early signs get minoxidil, oral finasteride and combination plans; Patchy, Extensive and reduced-density pictures keep only two unnamed SKUs; women: shedding gets cosmetic Hair Shedding Drops, other common pictures get the main SKU PHI1749); (3) mild scalp symptoms swap hair-loss plans for "Healthy Scalp" plans; (4) single allergies remove the matching active; men 50+ with Early signs or Temples lose oral finasteride. Family history, density for the common pictures, onset timing within gradual loss, medicines, other allergies, menopause and HRT change nothing. Women's hair type and styling answers only pick a haircare add-on. All of this was checked in 47 stage 2 and 22 stage 3 live replays by running the site's own rule function at the wall (every one matched the served rules, which were byte-identical to the saved copy on 24 Nov 2026); the results screen itself needs an account, and it comes before any result, so nobody learns their route (even a £200+ consultation) until they have registered.
strengths: One transparent, simple triage: every product has explicit safety blockers, and anyone who trips one is routed to a paid trichologist consultation rather than refused.
Consultation fallback is a real service with a calendar (virtual or clinic; trichologist or senior trichologist; male or female consultant).
Scalp-first approach: mild scalp symptoms swap hair-loss plans for "Healthy Scalp" plans; severe symptoms go to a consultation; a separate scalp quiz exists.
Women have their own quiz with a shedding route (cosmetic Hair Shedding Drops) and a haircare add-on chosen from hair type, length and styling: a natural upsell.

Strong safety coverage for a short quiz: cancer/PSA, depression with a specific finasteride mood warning, trying for a baby, pregnancy, chemotherapy and oral minoxidil are all screened before any product.
Men must confirm on the start screen that the finasteride and minoxidil products are unlicensed; leaflets say they are made under pharmacist supervision.
weaknesses: Account wall before any result: name, date of birth, email and password are taken before the person learns whether they get a plan or must pay £200-£345 for a consultation. The wall screen is identical for both routes (44 live variants checked).

Configuration errors in the served rules: the blood-pressure blocker has a leading space, so men who tick uncontrolled low or high blood pressure are still offered minoxidil 5% and the combination plans (live runs/m25); the 3% Combination Plan can never be offered; PHI1230 and PHI1770-1772 can never fire; label typos ("curerrently", "redness??").

Women: sudden loss with a widening parting is not escalated (live runs/w09), while the same change with overall thinning is (runs/w10); menopause and HRT answers are unused; no finasteride product is ever offered to women online.

Thin clinical screen: no under-18 answer (age bands start at 18; the women's quiz asks no age at all), one tick-box for blood pressure, no heart, kidney, liver or sexual side-effect questions; medicines and allergies are free text that no rule reads.

Men with Patchy, Extensive or reduced-density loss, or psoriasis/redness, are not routed to a consultation in the rules; they keep two unnamed SKUs (PHI1220, PHI1221). Whether these are still sold decides what they see.
Family history and hair density do not change the offer for the common male pictures, and the women's "how noticeable" follow-ups are never used: questions that look diagnostic are decoration.
Mixed messages: the men's page says "FULLY LICENSED" while leaflets say unlicensed; prices differ between pages (oral finasteride £40 vs £42; virtual consultation from £150 vs from £200).
Who prescribes is not stated anywhere public (trichologists are not prescribers; leaflets only say "pharmacist supervision").
opportunities: Show the route (plan or consultation, and its price) before asking for an account. PK makes people register before they find out they owe £200+.

Offer a cheaper middle route for the people PK sends to a £200-£345 consultation (sudden shedding, mild-to-moderate scalp symptoms, patchy loss): a prescriber review with photos at a fixed lower price.

A prescriber-led women's offer: PK sells women only a minoxidil-type drop or cosmetic shedding drops online; no oral minoxidil, spironolactone or topical finasteride for post-menopausal women, and menopause answers are ignored.
Use the answers PK collects but ignores (family history, density, menopause, medicines) to personalise strength and expectations: an easy way to look more clinical.
Clear licensing and prescriber information, and a blood-pressure and heart screen that actually works, as trust signals against a premium brand whose rules contain visible mistakes.

verification.verdict: Trustworthy as labelled for what the quiz asks and how its rules decide. The served rule set was byte-identical to the saved copy, the three baselines reproduced exactly, and 19 more live replays (12 on options nobody had tested) each matched an independent port of the site's own rule check, so every "code" rule in this file can be relied on as a description of the client-side engine on 24 Nov 2026. No rule was contradicted. The main errors found were labelling, not substance: option effect types that called a severity follow-up a hard stop, prices attributed to a screen that does not show them, a few assumptions written as fact, one wrong audience and two missing cosmetic products; all are fixed. The real limit is the account wall: nobody has seen the rendered results page, and six SKUs (including the women's main product PHI1749) remain unnamed, so "what product a person finally sees" is a strong code-based prediction, not an observation.
